startup_smoke.conclusion: All three isolated launches reached a stable renderer. No controlled pre-slim timing was captured, so this ticket makes no startup speed-up claim.

allowlist.name: sql
allowlist.reason: DBCode activates on the sql language and the wrapper opens SQL query documents; Code OSS has no SQL language registration without this extension.

allowlist.name: theme-defaults
allowlist.reason: The current Code OSS default Dark 2026 color theme is supplied here, so retaining it preserves the approved shell colors and contrast.

allowlist.name: theme-seti
allowlist.reason: Code OSS selects vs-seti as its default file icon theme, so retaining it preserves the approved SQL tab and document icon appearance.

allowlist.name: notebook-renderers
allowlist.reason: DBCode renders its private notebook MIME type itself, while this small fallback renders standard text, error, image, and stream outputs in DBCode notebooks.

allowlist.name: python
allowlist.reason: DBCode Python cells need Code OSS's declarative Python language registration; the external Python extension supplies runtime discovery but intentionally does not duplicate this grammar.

allowlist.name: ipynb
allowlist.reason: The focused Python-kernel bridge needs Code OSS's small Jupyter-notebook serializer so it can start a user-selected kernel for DBCode without exposing a general notebook workbench.

first_party.name: dbcode-wrapper-python-kernel
first_party.reason: The focused bridge starts a user-selected Jupyter kernel for DBCode Python cells without exposing a general Jupyter workbench.

first_party.name: dbcode-wrapper-release-status
first_party.reason: The focused bridge reports official host and DBCode release metadata without exposing an extension marketplace or automatic updater.

first_party.name: dbcode-wrapper-profile-migration
first_party.reason: The focused first-run bridge verifies and installs the pinned external runtime on a fresh Mac, then reviews non-secret connection details without reading another editor profile or secret store.

removed_groups.reason: These extensions provide non-SQL grammars, language servers, configuration editors, and generic search or diff helpers that are outside the DBCode-focused product.
Markdown previews, Mermaid rendering, media preview, and the simple browser are general IDE surfaces and are not used by DBCode query or database webviews.
Git, GitHub, JavaScript debugging, task runners, merge helpers, terminal suggestions, and tunnel forwarding belong to the removed general IDE workbench.
The GitHub and Microsoft host authentication providers serve Code OSS accounts; DBCode owns its own account, licence, connection, and secret flows.
These optional themes are not selected by the managed product; theme-defaults retains the active color theme and theme-seti retains the active file icons.

rollback_paths.all_built_ins: Set build.built_in_extensions.mode to all and rebuild. This restores the upstream built-in payload without changing DBCode, its profile, licence, saved connections, or secrets.

notes: Installed size uses du -sk and is separate from compressed archive size.
The indicative archive uses COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar -czf and is not a release ZIP or DMG.
There are 93 real built-in extensions plus one shared extensions/node_modules directory; the earlier directory count of 94 included that shared dependency directory.
The external DBCode extension remains outside the app and is never slimmed by this policy.
The final signed app passed static, rendered, real-Keychain, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, Parquet, SQL-file, result-layout, quit, and relaunch checks.
